newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai government to allocate fifth EU tapioca quota.
newsitem.headline: Thai government to allocate fifth EU tapioca quota.

text.p: Thailand's commerce ministry will allocate a fifth lot of tapioca to fill an export quota to the European Union, a ministry official said on Wednesday.
Stock checking was scheduled to take place on November 5 and the results would be used to allocate the quota for the November 8-December 15 export period, he told Reuters.
Thai exporters are allocated tapioca export quotas according to the size of stocks they hold.
The commerce ministry initially planned to make only four allocations this year.
But the extra fifth lot was given to fill the quota and to encourage exporters to buy more tapioca roots from farmers and so boost the sagging price.

The total tapioca export quota to the EU this year is 5.25 million tonnes, 3.0 million of which was based on stocks, 1.5 million on past export performance. The ministry also reserved 750,000 tonnes for allocation at its discretion.
The ministry had so far approved 2.63 million tonnes of tapioca exports on the basis of stocks, the official said.
